steps: Identify the normal force exerted by the wall on the body: N = 100 N.
Calculate the maximum possible static friction: f_max = ̈ × N = 0.3 × 100 = 30 N.
Calculate the downward gravitational force acting on the body: W = mg = 2 kg × 10 m/s² = 20 N.
Since the required force to hold the body (20 N) is less than the maximum static friction (30 N), the body remains stationary.
Therefore, the static frictional force adjusts to exactly balance the downward force: f = 20 N.
